subject: Clarify DPA and BYOK operator scenarios for private deployment
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidhealth.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <devops@orchidhealth.com>, Mark Chen <mark.chen@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA + BYOK operator scenarios for private deployment

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the walkthrough on Friday. We're onboarding a pilot of Redwood Private (VPC) and legal/security asked for a short write-up that maps the DPA obligations to concrete operator access scenarios for BYOK/on‑prem key custody. High-level asks: 

- A simple matrix that shows who (Redwood operator / customer admin / customer key custodian) has which capabilities in each deployment model (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC private).
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will appear in the subprocessor list for the private deployment variants and what processing activities that covers.
- Clarify whether operator troubleshooting ever requires plaintext model inputs stored in memory or logs, and if so what safeguards and audit trails exist.
- Cross‑border transfer implications if we bring the control plane into our US account but the keystore remains on our side.

I'm attaching our preliminary risk register for context. Can you send a short doc or slide with a recommended DPA clause and an example operator access workflow we can show security?

Appreciate it — basic timeline: security review next Tues (26 Jul).

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Head of Security, Orchid Health
[sent from mobile]

Attachment: Orchid_Prelim_Risk_Register.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 13:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA + BYOK operator scenarios for private deployment

Sarah —

Thanks, and great to partner on this. Attached is a concise package: 1) redwood_dpa_byok_options_v1.pdf (two recommended DPA clause variants: one for fully customer-controlled keys with minimal operator privileges, one for a hybrid where Redwood runs non-crypto operations), and 2) operator_access_matrix.xlsx (the matrix you asked for). Key points up front: 

- For VPC/on‑prem private deployments with BYOK, Redwood does not retain key material. Customer-managed keystore (KMS/HSM) keeps keys; Redwood's control plane(s) authenticate to an ephemeral service principal for orchestration only.
- Operator troubleshooting: the runtime can capture ephemeral plaintext in memory while processing a request. We avoid persistent plaintext logs in normal operation. Any exception path that requires operator access to request contents is governed by: documented break-glass procedure, dual-authorization, recorded session auditing, and a narrow time window. Example wording is in the attached PDF (see section "Operator Break‑Glass and Audit Trail").
- Subprocessor visibility: for private deployments we list the relevant subprocessors that touch the control plane (monitoring, telemetry, build pipeline). We propose an explicit carveout in the DPA Annex: customer-controlled keystore operations are not considered processing by Redwood for the purposes of customer data custody.
- Cross‑border transfers: if the control plane is in a different region, we recommend a data flow clause that (a) limits metadata replication, (b) prohibits full request body replication without customer consent, and (c) binds to a processor addendum restricting export outside the EU/US depending on your needs.

Next steps: 1) internal review with our privacy team (Karthik + Priyom) to finalize language, 2) send a short 1‑page summary for Orchid security, 3) propose a 30‑minute follow-up call next week to walk through the matrix.

I've CC'd Karthik and Priyom to confirm technical accuracy; Irene, please flag any legal concerns.

Attachments: redwood_dpa_byok_options_v1.pdf (doc stub), operator_access_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Jonas — quick tech notes for the doc and the clause variants: 

- "No plaintext retention" is accurate for steady state, but during live debugging we instantiate per-request buffers that contain plaintext for up to ~90 seconds. Recommend we document: 60–120s in-memory buffer, zero-written disk policy, mandatory ephemeral IDs for any capture, and automatic scrub within 5 minutes.
- Telemetry: redact sensitive fields in sampling pipeline; don't treat telemetry recipients as having data access to request body unless explicitly included in subprocessor list.
- Subprocessor list: include build CI, image registry, and monitoring provider. For private VPC: monitoring agents can be customer-deployed; propose alternate language that gives customers option to host telemetry collectors in their VPC.

Suggested addition to the DPA clause (short): "Redwood shall not access, persist, or export customer plaintext data from customer-controlled keystores except under mutually agreed break-glass procedures that require written customer authorization and dual Redwood approvals; all such access shall be logged and made available to customer within three business days."

I'll add a short tech annex to operator_access_matrix.xlsx after lunch and share a redline. Priyom — can you confirm whether our control plane backup snapshots include metadata that could be considered personal data? If so, we'll add a mitigation.

Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
